purpose: Public governance contract for keeping Moral Trade decisioning deterministic, schema-bound, documented, and human-controlled before any ML-assisted ranking or scoring is introduced.

requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.label: Model card
requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.rule: Any model used beyond rendering deterministic factor codes must publish intended use, non-use, risk, performance slices, and failure modes.

requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.label: Dataset datasheet
requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.rule: Any historical training or evaluation dataset must document collection, consent, composition, retention, exclusion rules, and known limitations.

requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.label: Benchmark slices
requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.rule: Benchmarks must include cause-area, trade-format, geography, privacy-stage, and optional governed sensitive-attribute slices.

requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.label: Intended-use limits
requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.rule: Documentation must state that the model cannot rank global moral value, make safety decisions, disclose counterparties, or complete agreements.

requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.label: Fairness audit report
requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.rule: Before rollout, publish aggregate fairness metrics, trade-offs, reviewed deviations, and remediation decisions.

requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.label: Change log
requiredDocumentationBeforeMl.rule: Every material model, dataset, prompt, or metric change must have an operator-visible change log entry and rollback note.

permittedAutomation.label: Schema-bound drafting
permittedAutomation.rule: Drafting may normalize user text into approved proposal fields without inventing facts or evidence.

permittedAutomation.label: Missing-field detection
permittedAutomation.rule: Automation may flag missing required fields and ask clarification questions tied to those fields.

permittedAutomation.label: Factor-code explanation rendering
permittedAutomation.rule: Automation may render explanations only from deterministic factor codes and approved redaction rules.

permittedAutomation.label: Evidence checklist drafting
permittedAutomation.rule: Automation may draft checklists of observable artifacts without deciding that evidence is sufficient.

permittedAutomation.label: Reviewer-summary drafting
permittedAutomation.rule: Automation may summarize records for reviewers while preserving uncertainty and unresolved flags.

prohibitedUses.label: End-to-end LLM matching
prohibitedUses.rule: No model may decide counterparties or matchability from broad application context.

prohibitedUses.label: Global moral ranking
prohibitedUses.rule: No model or optimization layer may claim a platform-wide objective moral ranking.

prohibitedUses.label: Unreviewed learning to rank
prohibitedUses.rule: Historical outcome ranking cannot be used until labels, bias risks, model cards, and fairness audits are complete.

prohibitedUses.label: Protected-trait inference
prohibitedUses.rule: Models must not infer protected traits, ideology, psychology, or hidden preferences for matching.

prohibitedUses.label: Autonomous outreach
prohibitedUses.rule: No automation may contact or reveal counterparties without explicit consent and human-controlled disclosure.

prohibitedUses.label: Raw private-feed training
prohibitedUses.rule: Raw private wishes, source notes, contact details, and private feeds cannot be used as model training input.

fairnessDocumentation.reviewRule: Material slice gaps must be thresholded, reviewed, documented, and remediated before promotion.

explanationControls.label: Factor codes are the source of truth
explanationControls.rule: Natural-language explanations may render deterministic factor codes and cited fields, but must not become a separate reasoning source.

explanationControls.label: Meaningful user action
explanationControls.rule: Every explanation must state the current status, why the deterministic factors led there, and what action the participant or reviewer can take next.

explanationControls.label: System accuracy boundary
explanationControls.rule: Explanations must be accurate to the system inputs: source fields, factor codes, evidence rows, and policy flags, without claiming hidden context or objective moral truth.

explanationControls.label: Uncertainty and redaction notice
explanationControls.rule: Explanations must name uncertainty flags and redacted surfaces when private wishes, contact details, sensitive constraints, or evidence remain hidden.

explanationControls.label: Appealable review scope
explanationControls.rule: Reviewer-facing explanations must state which claim, evidence row, or policy flag can be appealed and which unrelated moral disagreements are out of scope.

explanationControls.label: Reversible interaction
explanationControls.rule: Explanations must support correction, resubmission, or human override before state changes; users can correct fields without automatic disclosure or reliance.

externalStandards.label: NIST AI RMF
externalStandards.use: Govern, map, measure, and manage any model-assisted workflow before rollout.

externalStandards.label: NIST XAI principles
externalStandards.use: Require explanations that are meaningful, accurate to the system, bounded, and uncertainty-aware.

externalStandards.label: Model Cards
externalStandards.use: Document model purpose, limits, performance, risks, and non-use cases.

externalStandards.label: Datasheets for Datasets
externalStandards.use: Document dataset collection, consent, composition, retention, and limitations.

externalStandards.label: Fairness trade-off literature
externalStandards.use: Avoid pretending one fairness metric is universally correct; publish trade-offs and review decisions.
